title: Planning applications, sign variances and heritage district draft
subtitle: Official Plan update, 132 Clair Road West review, 1 Clair Road East approval, and a farewell to the deputy CAO
overview: Council spent the evening on planning matters. It approved the Official Plan and zoning changes for 1 Clair Road East, a mixed-use redevelopment of a shopping centre site {{vote:m16}}. It also asked that feedback from the rezoning process, including concerns about the internal north-south street and Poppy Drive traffic, be considered at site plan approval {{vote:m17}}.

Council approved two ground sign variances at 705 Southgate Drive after first defeating staff's recommended refusals {{vote:m13}}. A reduced separation distance between the two signs was also approved {{vote:m10}}. On the consent agenda, council extended two subdivision draft plan approvals to 2028 and passed a support resolution for rooftop solar projects {{vote:m2}}.

Three items were received only, so no decisions were made on them. These were the draft Downtown Heritage Conservation District plan {{vote:m6}}, Phase 1 of the Official Plan update {{vote:m7}}, and the public meeting on 132 Clair Road West {{vote:m8}}. Final decisions on the first two are expected in early 2026. After a closed session on an employment land acquisition, the mayor reported that council gave staff direction. The meeting was also the last for the deputy CAO of Infrastructure, Development and Environment.

decisions.detail: Council approved the Official Plan and zoning amendments allowing higher density, a site-specific commercial mixed-use zone and a neighbourhood park at the corner of Hawkins Drive and Poppy Drive East.
Council directed that feedback from the zoning amendment process be considered during site plan approval for the property.
Council approved variances for two ground signs at 705 Southgate Drive, with setbacks of 3 metres and 1 metre, a 7.5 metre height and a 12.78 square metre sign face.
Council approved a variance allowing about 80 metres between the two ground signs on the Southgate Drive property.
Council extended the draft plan approval for 1159 Victoria Road South for three years, to November 22, 2028, with updated conditions.
Council extended the draft plan approval for 635 Woodlawn Road East for three years, to November 18, 2028, with updated conditions.
Council supported a proposal for rooftop solar projects at several city industrial-area addresses, a resolution required for the provincial energy procurement process.
Council received draft Official Plan Amendment No. 110, which aligns the plan with provincial policy and the transportation and parks master plans.

debate: On the Downtown Heritage District, a delegate raised concerns about mortgage and insurance availability, possible future permit fees, maintenance costs and unclear guidelines. Staff said permits are free, many repairs are exempt, and the plan does not require rebuilding after a loss. Several councillors said they had not heard of such problems in the existing heritage district and asked for the 2021 survey to be shared.

Some councillors worried the heritage district could become another layer of rules on downtown building height and could hold back intensification. Staff said the examples followed the heights already approved in the downtown plan. One councillor said the gap between delegates' experience and staff's findings should be explored before the final plan returns.

On 132 Clair Road West, several councillors said the request for up to 250 units per hectare and 14 stories, on land not in a strategic growth area, was more than minor zoning relief. They also questioned the reduced garage and lot sizes, the lack of affordability commitments and the reduced amenities. The applicant said the density was meant to allow flexibility, shifted from other blocks, and that it was open to changes. Staff will address this in the final report.

On the Southgate Drive signs, staff recommended refusing the taller signs, saying they did not follow council's sign by-law and could prompt more variance requests. The delegate argued that height was needed for safety and visibility near a hard-to-see entrance and a fence. Most councillors accepted this because the site is commercial and away from homes.

On 1 Clair Road East, one councillor proposed limiting the internal street to service and emergency access because nearby residents worried about Poppy Drive traffic. Staff said traffic engineers had reviewed it, that it was premature at rezoning, and that it would be reviewed at site plan. The amendment was defeated {{vote:m15}}.
